articles.title: Could Aaron Donald still dominate for the Rams? Why an NFL comeback might be more realistic than many think
articles.standfirst: The juggernaut was still one of the best defensive players in football when he retired in 2023
articles.summary: The juggernaut was still one of the best defensive players in football when he retired in 2023
articles.body:
Few questions in football are more fascinating right now than this one: Can Aaron Donald still make an impact if he returns to the NFL? For most retired players, the answer would be easy. A two-year absence from football at age 35 would typically end any discussion about elite-level performance.

Aaron Donald is not most players. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year has become the subject of growing comeback speculation throughout the summer, with reports indicating he has continued training and even worked out with the Los Angeles Rams as he weighs a possible return. Rams head coach Sean McVay has done little to cool the rumors, openly acknowledging that Donald could still be effective if he decided to come back.

The bigger question is whether he could still be Aaron Donald. The strongest argument in favor of a comeback is simple: Donald wasn't declining when he retired. When he walked away following the 2023 season, he was still one of the best defensive players in football.

He finished that year with eight sacks, earned another Pro Bowl selection, and was named First-Team All-Pro for the eighth time in his career. Most NFL legends retire because their bodies no longer allow them to perform at a high level.

Donald retired because he no longer wanted the grind

Reports throughout 2026 have suggested that Donald has remained in excellent shape and has continued on-field work while considering a return. Multiple NFL insiders have described a comeback as a legitimate possibility rather than a publicity stunt. And if he returns, he would be stepping into perhaps the most favorable situation of his career.

Myles Garrett changes everything. During Donald's prime, opposing offenses often built entire game plans around stopping him. Now imagine offensive coordinators trying to handle Donald and Myles Garrett on the same defensive front. The Rams' blockbuster acquisition of Garrett has dramatically altered the equation. Sean McVay recently joked that if Donald decides to "dust them off" at age 35, he could still perform "at a pretty high clip."

He's probably right. Donald would no longer need to be the centerpiece of every defensive game plan. Garrett's presence would create one-on-one opportunities that Donald rarely enjoyed during his first stint in Los Angeles. For the first time in years, Donald might actually face fewer double teams than the players around him. That's a terrifying thought for quarterbacks.

Of course, there are legitimate reasons for caution because football is different from training. Donald has not played in an NFL game since the Rams' playoff loss following the 2023 season. By the time he takes the field again, nearly three years will have passed since his last meaningful snap.

History is not especially kind to players returning after multi-year retirements. The physical demands of playing defensive tackle are immense. Conditioning can be rebuilt. Timing, reaction speed, and the ability to withstand constant collisions are much harder to replicate outside of live competition.

Even supporters of a comeback acknowledge that expecting the 2018 version of Aaron Donald would be unrealistic. The player who once routinely posted double-digit sacks while facing constant double teams may not exist anymore. But that doesn't mean he can't still be highly effective.

The Rams don't need Donald to be the best defensive player in football. They need him to be a productive one. Even if Donald returns at 80 percent of his peak level, he would likely remain one of the better interior defensive linemen in the NFL . His technique, leverage, football intelligence, and hand usage have always separated him from other players. Those skills don't disappear overnight.

articles.title: How Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant helped Myles Garrett develop ‘killer instinct’ on the field
articles.standfirst: The Rams star explained why Bryant’s ruthless approach still influences how he prepares to dominate NFL opponents
articles.summary: The Rams star explained why Bryant’s ruthless approach still influences how he prepares to dominate NFL opponents
articles.body:
Myles Garrett has spent his career terrorizing NFL quarterbacks, but the mindset behind that dominance was shaped partly by an athlete who made his name on a basketball court in Los Angeles.

Now preparing for his first season with the Los Angeles Rams , Garrett has revealed how Lakers legend Kobe Bryant became one of the sporting figures he studied while developing the mentality that helped turn him into one of football’s most feared defenders.

Appearing on “Boardroom Talks,” Garrett grouped Bryant alongside NFL icon Lawrence Taylor and NBA great Michael Jordan as athletes whose competitive instincts separated them from everyone around them.

“You get to see the duality of it,” Garrett said. “You have [Lawrence Taylor], you have Kobe, you have [Michael Jordan], who have a killer instinct. It exudes from them. They want to kill you, want to take you out the game.”

Bryant built his reputation around that relentless competitive approach during 20 seasons with the Lakers. His “Mamba Mentality” became shorthand for obsessive preparation, resilience and an unwillingness to accept anything below his own standards.

Garrett believes that same combination of aggression and freedom can be transferred to football.

Kobe Bryant mentality left mark on Garrett

“Just playing the game as freely as you can, trying to combine the two,” Garrett said. “That’s how I feel like I walk on the field. I walk on the field and I plan to destroy the game, but I plan to have fun doing it the whole time.”

Bryant ’s career provided countless examples of that mentality. He won five NBA championships, became an 18-time All-Star and twice led the league in scoring.

One of his most memorable displays of toughness came in 2013, when he remained on the court long enough to make two free throws after suffering a torn Achilles.

Three years later, Bryant closed his career by scoring 60 points against the Utah Jazz in his final game at Staples Center.

Garrett also pointed to Muhammad Ali as another major influence, particularly because of the heavyweight champion’s ability to defeat opponents psychologically as well as physically.

“Once you start playing those mental games and doing that mental gymnastics, you’re already defeated,” Garrett said. “Then he’s got you right where he wants you.”

Those influences help explain the mentality Garrett is now bringing to Los Angeles.

Rams hope Garrett’s mentality leads to Super Bowl

The Rams acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns during the offseason after another remarkable individual campaign in which he recorded 23 sacks, surpassing Michael Strahan ’s long-standing single-season record.

His introduction to Los Angeles has been deliberately cautious, however, with knee soreness limiting his participation throughout training camp.

“I feel good,” Garrett said earlier in August. “I'm allowed to get sore. I'm a little old.”

Head coach Sean McVay has insisted the Rams are prioritizing Garrett ’s availability for the regular season rather than pushing him through meaningless preseason work.

“We are, yeah,” McVay said when asked whether Los Angeles was being cautious. “The goal is, what can we do to be able to get him ready to roll for Australia? That's kind of where you see that approach.”

Garrett has already conquered most individual challenges available to an NFL pass rusher. The next one is considerably bigger.

Los Angeles brought him in to help chase a Super Bowl, and Garrett appears ready to attack that objective with a mentality borrowed from one of the city’s greatest sporting icons.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Alert: Possible suspension of Puka Nacua on the Rams could be major problem
articles.standfirst: A potential suspension creates risk around the Rams receiver
articles.summary: A potential suspension creates risk around the Rams receiver
articles.body:
Puka Nacua ’s fantasy value has become one of the trickiest calls of draft season, not because anything has changed about his talent, but because managers still don't know whether he will be available when the Los Angeles Rams open the NFL regular season.

Nacua is coming off a dominant year in which he led the NFL with 129 receptions, finished second with 1,715 receiving yards and scored 10 touchdowns. That production made him fantasy football’s No.1 wide receiver.

Normally, those numbers would make him an easy first-round selection. The complication is the possibility of NFL discipline stemming from several off-field matters that remain under review.

No suspension has been announced, but ESPN insider Adam Schefter made clear earlier this month that missing the opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia remains possible.

“[Nacua] could potentially face discipline for some of the offseason headlines that accompanied him,” Schefter said.

He added: “It’s possible that when the 49ers and Rams play in Australia, it’s within the realm of options that Puka doesn’t play in that game.”

That uncertainty should matter in fantasy drafts. It shouldn't, however, trigger a collapse in Nacua ’s value.

Short suspension would barely dent Nacua’s upside

Fantasy managers should separate the risk of a suspension from the severity of one.

If Nacua misses only Week 1, his season-long value remains extremely strong. Passing on a player capable of delivering 1,700 receiving yards because of a single absence could end up being an overreaction.

Even a two-game suspension wouldn't necessarily push him outside the first round. The calculation changes if the NFL announces something more significant.

A four-game absence would make Nacua much harder to justify among the top three or four overall selections, particularly when Ja’Marr Chase and other elite receivers offer similar ceilings without the same availability concern.

Until there is clarity, the safest approach is to move Nacua down a few spots rather than several rounds.

If he reaches the back half of Round 1, the value becomes much easier to defend. If nervous managers allow him to fall into Round 2, the risk may be worth embracing.

Fantasy managers should build around uncertainty

Anyone drafting Nacua should have a contingency plan. Using another early selection on a reliable wide receiver can protect against a short-term absence and prevent a roster from becoming too dependent on one player.

Davante Adams is another major weapon in the Rams offense, while Los Angeles’ decision to bring Tutu Atwell back has created further speculation about Nacua’s status. That move alone, though, isn't evidence that a suspension is imminent.

Nacua remains one of the most dangerous fantasy assets on the board. The smartest move is not to pretend the suspension risk does not exist. It is to price that risk correctly.

Until the NFL announces significant discipline, Nacua still belongs in the first-round conversation. If he slips much further, the uncertainty could turn into somebody else’s best draft-night bargain.

articles.title: Rams' Aaron Donald's two-word message to Commissioner Roger Goodell should terrify the rest of the NFL
articles.standfirst: Donald is back with the Los Angeles Rams for the 2026 season, with another Super Bowl ring in mind.
articles.summary: Donald is back with the Los Angeles Rams for the 2026 season, with another Super Bowl ring in mind.
articles.body:
It's official: Aaron Donald has unretired and is once again a member of the Los Angeles Rams . Donald's return had been teased nearly all offseason, but it finally came to fruition with the season less than two weeks way.

Donald will join Myles Garrett , Matthew Stafford , Puka Nacua , and more stars on a truly stacked Rams roster. At this point, Los Angeles is the overwhelming favorite to win the Super Bowl . Whether that happens or not, though, Donald coming back and dominating at age 35 after over two years out of football would be truly special.

Aaron Donald channels Michael Jordan in return statement

For those doubting whether Donald can do that, his physique in workout videos should say enough. But in case they don't, Donald made sure to make a short but strong statement on the day of his return . He sent a message indicating his return to the NFL to Commissioner Roger Goodell with only two words: " I'm Back ".

Donald marked his return with his first official practice as a Rams member later in the day. The defensive lineman kept things relatively simple, running light drills . It was a walkthrough day for the Rams , although Donald probably wouldn't have gone full blast even if it wasn't.

The Rams ended up giving Donald a one-year contract worth $20 million , that could go all the way up to $30 million with incentives . If it does go all the way up, it means Donald returned to his usual self this season, which would be a major win for the Rams.

articles.title: Aaron Donald's wife reveals surprising reason behind his Rams comeback
articles.standfirst: Family played a major role in the Rams legend's unexpected return.
articles.summary: Family played a major role in the Rams legend's unexpected return.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald's return to the Los Angeles Rams came as a surprise across the NFL, but his wife Erica has now revealed that the decision was driven by something far more personal than unfinished business on the field.

Donald had stepped away from football after the 2023 season, ending a Hall-of-Fame-level career that included three Defensive Player of the Year awards and a Super Bowl title.

But after spending time away from the game, the former defensive tackle ultimately decided he still wanted another chapter with Los Angeles.

Aaron Donald's family helped change his mind

Erica Donald explained that retirement gave her husband something he hadn't experienced much during his playing career: extended time at home with his family.

"He got a chance to really be a dad," she said.

That time away appears to have changed his perspective rather than completely satisfying his desire to remain retired.

According to Erica , the family became an important part of the conversation when Donald began considering a comeback.

"The kids were like, 'Dad, we want to see you play,'" she said.

That reaction helped push Donald toward returning to the Rams , where he had spent his entire NFL career before retiring.

Rams legend still had football left in him

Erica also made clear that Donald hadn't completely lost his competitive edge during retirement.

"He missed football," she said.

The combination of family encouragement and his own desire to compete again eventually became enough to bring him back.

Donald had previously spoken about wanting to leave the game while still physically capable of performing at an elite level rather than waiting until his body forced him out.

His return now gives the Rams one of the most dominant defensive players of his generation back in the middle of their front.

There will naturally be questions about how quickly Donald can regain his previous level after time away, but the motivation behind the comeback appears clear.

This wasn't simply about chasing another contract or adding to an already remarkable resume.

Donald had spent retirement enjoying life as a father, but when his children told him they wanted to watch him play again, it helped reopen a door many assumed had been permanently closed.

articles.title: Gisele Bundchen gets dragged back into NFL debate after Aaron Donald's Rams return
articles.standfirst: Aaron Donald's comeback unexpectedly revived comparisons with Tom Brady's retirement saga.
articles.summary: Aaron Donald's comeback unexpectedly revived comparisons with Tom Brady's retirement saga.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald's return to the Los Angeles Rams has unexpectedly dragged Gisele Bundchen back into the NFL conversation years after her divorce from Tom Brady .

The three-time Defensive Player of the Year came out of retirement after agreeing to a one-year, $20 million deal with the Rams .

His wife, Erica Donald , immediately celebrated the decision on social media.

"I let him out of the house y'all," Erica wrote alongside laughing and heart emojis.

That prompted NFL insider Clarence Hill Jr . to make a pointed comparison with Brady's former marriage.

"If only Gisele Bundchen had been equally supportive," Hill wrote.

Gisele Bundchen gets pulled back into old Tom Brady debate

The comment reopened discussion around Brady's brief 2022 retirement and subsequent return to football.

Brady initially retired saying he wanted to spend more time with his family, only to reverse the decision six weeks later.

Bundchen publicly supported Brady , but she later expressed concerns about his return to the NFL. Reports also emerged that the couple were experiencing marital problems before they filed for divorce in October 2022.

That history made Hill's comparison inevitable, although Donald's situation appears very different.

Aaron Donald credits wife Erica for comeback

Donald made clear that his own return wouldn't have happened without his wife's approval.

"I think my wife played a huge part in this, me making this decision, period," Donald said. "Because, if the wife wasn't happy, it wasn't gonna get done. We gotta make sure that the household was good. The kid was okay with it all, having them hard conversations, figuring things out. What I wanted to do, if I was gonna do it, how would we do it."

He said Erica ultimately gave him her full backing.

"So, my wife was onboard. She said, 'If you wanna do this, just put your 100%.' ... She played a huge part in me figuring this out because it really wasn't an easy decision."

Donald first met Erica in 2015 while she was working for the Rams, and the couple later married privately.

His comeback may belong entirely to the Donald family, but one social media comparison was enough to bring Bundchen and Brady's old retirement drama back into the NFL spotlight.

articles.title: Trouble for the Rams: Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett could miss Week 1
articles.standfirst: Los Angeles wants Garrett ready for Australia, but the team is taking no chances with his knee
articles.summary: Los Angeles wants Garrett ready for Australia, but the team is taking no chances with his knee
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams built their defense around the idea of unleashing Myles Garrett alongside Aaron Donald . With the season opener approaching, however, the first question is whether Garrett will be ready to take the field at all.

The reigning Defensive Player of the Year has spent much of the summer managing swelling in his knee and has been a full participant in practice only twice.

That has made his status one of the biggest storylines surrounding Los Angeles ahead of its Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

Sean McVay has now provided the clearest indication yet of what the Rams are working toward.

“He’s making good progress. Really good progress,” McVay said Monday. “The goal all along has been Australia.”

Garrett ’s limited practice work has naturally created concern, especially after the Rams expected him to return last week and he remained sidelined.

McVay , though, has continued to frame the situation as caution rather than setback.

Rams not willing to gamble Garrett’s season

Garrett arrived in Los Angeles after leading the NFL with 23 sacks in 2025, and the Rams paid heavily to acquire one of the league’s most dominant defensive players.

That makes the temptation to get him on the field immediately obvious.

McVay insists the organization will not allow the excitement surrounding the opener to override Garrett ’s long-term health.

“If he’s not ready, and that’s not what’s best for him and the team, absolutely wouldn’t have him play in Australia,” McVay said.

That approach makes sense for a player expected to anchor the defense over an entire season rather than simply provide a spectacle in Week 1.

The Rams also named Garrett one of their captains, underlining how quickly he has become a central figure despite missing considerable practice time.

Donald’s return adds more uncertainty

The intrigue has only increased following Donald ’s decision to come out of retirement.

The prospect of Garrett and Donald lining up together has immediately transformed expectations for the Rams ’ defensive front, but Donald is also being eased back after two seasons away from football.

He didn't practice Monday, instead working in the weight room as part of what the team described as a planned progression.

articles.title: Which NFL teams finished the preseason undefeated? Recent history offers a warning as we head into the 2026 season
articles.standfirst: Since 2021, only 10 of the 25 teams that remained unbeaten in pre-season made it to the play-offs
articles.summary: Since 2021, only 10 of the 25 teams that remained unbeaten in pre-season made it to the play-offs
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is right around the corner, and in the NFC , there is a clear favorite in the Los Angeles Rams , not only because Super Bowl 61 will be played at their home venue, SoFi Stadium where they captured their last Lombardi Trophy four seasons ago, or because they feature an elite offense led by reigning MVP Matthew Stafford , Puka Nacua , and Davante Adams .

The primary reason for their powerhouse status is their defense, bolstered by a blockbuster trade for reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett , who is coming off a record-breaking sack campaign.

They also acquired star cornerback Trent McDuffie , alongside the stunning return of 3x Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald , who at 35 years old came out of retirement on a 1-year, $20 million deal to pair with Garrett in forming arguably the most terrifying pass-rushing duo in league history.

Preseason Perfection Meets History: Why Unbeaten Augusts Spell Danger for NFL Contenders

In theory, the biggest challengers to the Rams in the NFC are the defending champion Seattle Seahawks , but unlike the Rams, who swept their three preseason matchups against the Chiefs, Saints, and Chargers, the Seahawks failed to win a single exhibition contest while suffering more major roster departures than incoming signings during the offseason.

The Rams managed to finish the preseason undefeated alongside the Buffalo Bills , Baltimore Ravens , and Cincinnati Bengals . While all four squads look like heavy playoff locks on paper, recent history issues a stark warning.

Ever since the preseason slate was reduced from four games to three starting in 2021, 25 teams have finished the exhibition schedule undefeated, but only 10 of them managed to punch their ticket to the postseason, representing a modest 40% success rate .

Even more telling, out of those 25 unbeaten preseason squads, only the Denver Broncos managed to advance past the wild-card round last year.

For high-powered outfits like the Rams , Bills , Ravens , and Bengals , who are universally projected to contend for a Super Bowl title, the historical odds are strangely stacked against them. Looking closely at these trends, at least one of these four heavyweights is projected to miss the postseason entirely.

For the Bills and Rams , missing January football would register as an unmitigated disaster; for the Ravens , missing the playoffs in back-to-back seasons is something that has never occurred during the entire Lamar Jackson era; and for the Bengals , another postseason absence would mark four straight years without playoff football, applying immense pressure squarely onto Joe Burrow and the front office.

articles.title: New allegations hit Puka Nacua as ex-girlfriend speaks out on relationship trauma
articles.standfirst: Hallie Aiono described experiencing “extreme betrayal” and “abuse” during a four-year relationship with the Rams star, although she did not identify Nacua directly in her latest video
articles.summary: Hallie Aiono described experiencing “extreme betrayal” and “abuse” during a four-year relationship with the Rams star, although she did not identify Nacua directly in her latest video
articles.body:
P uka Nacua is facing another wave of scrutiny away from the football field after his former girlfriend, Hallie Aiono , spoke publicly about the emotional damage she says she experienced during their relationship.

Aiono discussed her decision to seek professional help for her mental health in a TikTok video posted Sunday night.

While she did not make a specific allegation against Nacua or identify him by name in the video, her description of a relationship that she says involved abuse has inevitably drawn attention because of her previous connection to the Los Angeles Rams wide receiver.

The development comes at an especially sensitive time for Nacua , who is already waiting to learn whether the NFL will discipline him over separate offseason incidents.

“I went from loving somebody so deeply for four years, I felt it in my bones, to experiencing extreme betrayal, abuse, complete neglect from them, in what felt like it happened almost overnight,” Aiono said.

She also explained that what happened away from the public eye had a particularly profound effect on her: “A lot of the things that were public affected my mental health. But honestly, the things that were happening in private are what completely crushed me and altered my brain chemistry. Those parts, what people never saw, or know of, are what broke me.”

Aiono's comments are not, by themselves, a formal accusation against Nacua , and she did not provide specific details in the video identifying what she meant by abuse. That distinction is important as the Rams receiver faces separate legal and league-related scrutiny.

The pair's relationship has already been the subject of considerable public attention. Aiono is the mother of Nacua's son, Kingston, and their personal circumstances became a major topic of discussion last year during a paternity dispute.

Aiono has also previously spoken about the emotional strain she experienced surrounding the pregnancy and the public commentary that followed.

In July, she addressed criticism stemming from comments made about her on The Pivot Podcast, saying that the discussion had taken a toll on her mental health.

Nacua's NFL situation remains unresolved

The latest development arrives while the NFL continues to review Nacua's off-field conduct.

The wide receiver is facing a civil lawsuit filed by Madison Atiabi , who alleges that Nacua assaulted and battered her during a New Year's Eve incident. The lawsuit includes claims of assault, battery, gender violence and negligence.

Nacua's attorney has disputed the allegations, describing the incident differently and denying accusations surrounding an alleged antisemitic remark.

The lawsuit has not resulted in a criminal conviction, and the allegations remain contested. However, the NFL's personal conduct policy allows the league to conduct its own review independent of the outcome of a civil case.

As of late August, Nacua had not been placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List. NBC Sports reported that neither Nacua nor Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson was placed on paid leave at that point, although the league's review remained ongoing.

That leaves uncertainty hanging over the Rams just days before the start of their regular season.

Nacua is coming off a spectacular 2025 campaign in which he established himself as one of the NFL's premier receivers.

He led the league with 129 receptions and finished with 1,715 receiving yards, making his potential availability especially important to a Los Angeles offense that also added veteran star Davante Adams .

The Rams have nevertheless continued preparing for the season with Nacua on their roster. He dealt with psoas soreness during training camp, but head coach Sean McVay expected him to return to practice after the issue forced him to leave a joint session with Dallas early.

Now, the bigger question is whether Nacua will be available when the games begin.

The Rams are scheduled to open their season against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, on Sept. 10. With the NFL's decision still pending, Nacua's status for that trip remains uncertain.

For Aiono , however, her latest comments were centered on a different issue: seeking help and addressing what she says has happened behind closed doors.

Her account has added another layer to an already complicated offseason for Nacua , but it is important to distinguish between her general description of abuse and any specific allegation against the receiver. No such specific allegation was made in the latest video.

For the Rams, the focus now shifts back to the NFL as the league weighs its response to Nacua's separate off-field issues with the season opener rapidly approaching.

articles.title: Myles Garrett and the Rams have the tools to terrorize the NFL. Are they the best defense in the league?
articles.standfirst: Lining up Myles with Aaron Donald on the same defensive front is enough to make offensive coordinators lose sleep
articles.summary: Lining up Myles with Aaron Donald on the same defensive front is enough to make offensive coordinators lose sleep
articles.body:
T he Los Angeles Rams spent the offseason assembling a defense that, on paper, looks more like an All-Star team than a traditional NFL roster. And according to NFL.com editor-at-large Gennaro Filice , no one benefited more from those moves than defensive coordinator Chris Shula.

After helping guide one of the NFL’s most promising young defenses over the past two seasons, Shula now finds himself with an embarrassment of riches. The Rams not only addressed key weaknesses but also added elite talent at every level of the defense, creating a unit that has the potential to become one of the league’s most dominant groups in 2026.

Filice recently highlighted just how dramatically the Rams transformed their defense during the offseason. The makeover began in March when Los Angeles strengthened its secondary by acquiring cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson from the Kansas City Chiefs. The move immediately upgraded a position group that had long been viewed as a vulnerability.

McDuffie arrived in Los Angeles with an impressive résumé. The former Chiefs standout won two Super Bowls during his time in Kansas City and earned multiple All-Pro selections while establishing himself as one of the NFL’s premier cover corners. Watson , meanwhile, brought championship experience and valuable versatility to the secondary.

The Rams did not stop there

In June, Los Angeles made perhaps the most significant defensive acquisition in football by trading for Myles Garrett . Widely regarded as the best defensive player in the NFL today, Garrett gives the Rams a game-changing force capable of taking over contests on his own. His combination of size, speed, power, and technique has made him one of the league’s most feared pass rushers, and his arrival instantly elevated expectations for the entire defense.

Then came the move that truly stunned the football world. In August, Aaron Donald returned to the Rams . The future Hall of Famer, widely considered one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history , rejoined the franchise where he built a legendary career and became the face of the organization’s defense for more than a decade.

The prospect of Donald and Garrett lining up on the same defensive front is enough to make offensive coordinators lose sleep. Garrett has spent years terrorizing quarterbacks as the focal point of opposing game plans. Donald did the same throughout his Hall of Fame career, routinely drawing double and triple teams while still producing at an elite level. Now, Shula has both players at his disposal.

Championships are not won on paper

On paper, the Rams’ defense resembles something out of a fantasy football draft. Elite pass rushers, championship-tested cornerbacks, and a respected coordinator entering the prime of his career have created enormous expectations in Los Angeles.

As Filice noted, there are still questions that can only be answered on the field. The Rams must determine how all the pieces fit together. Integrating star players, managing roles, and developing chemistry are challenges every talented roster faces. Talent alone does not guarantee dominance.

Still, few defensive coordinators enter the season with a better collection of weapons than Shula. The grandson of legendary coach Don Shula has steadily built a reputation as one of the NFL’s brightest defensive minds. Entering his third season as defensive coordinator, he now has the personnel to fully unleash his vision.

With Garrett generating pressure off the edge, Donald commanding attention inside, McDuffie l ocking down receivers in coverage, and Watson providing additional depth and versatility, the Rams possess the ingredients necessary to field the NFL’s most feared defense. If the unit performs anywhere close to its potential, Shula's name could soon be mentioned among the league's top head-coaching candidates.

articles.title: Rams QB Matthew Stafford’s wife Kelly makes honest ‘overstimulated mom’ confession
articles.standfirst: Wife of NFL MVP hopes her daughters remember a great childhood despite the chaos
articles.summary: Wife of NFL MVP hopes her daughters remember a great childhood despite the chaos
articles.body:
Kelly Stafford has spent enough years around the NFL to know what happens when the regular season begins.

The calendar tightens, Matthew Stafford ’s responsibilities with the Los Angeles Rams take over, and much of the day-to-day chaos of raising four daughters inevitably falls on her.

That reality was at the heart of a recent Instagram post in which Kelly shared a montage of family moments and summed up motherhood in unmistakably candid fashion.

“I hope one day when my kids are older, they look back and say ‘even though my mom was a overstimulated, raging psycho, she still gave us the best childhood.’ *and dad,” she wrote.

The joke was self-deprecating, but the sentiment behind it was clear. Kelly hopes daughters Chandler, Sawyer, Hunter and Tyler Hall remember the experiences their parents created for them rather than the stress that sometimes came with making those moments happen.

Never hidden the chaos behind family life

The Stafford family’s schedule has regularly required careful planning around Matthew ’s football commitments and the children’s own activities.

Kelly has previously spoken about one particularly stressful trip to Philadelphia when all four daughters had soccer games on the same day the family needed to catch a flight.

She has also discussed the more difficult sides of motherhood, including pregnancy and postpartum recovery, while generally keeping her public comments grounded in the reality that raising four children can be exhausting regardless of the circumstances.

Her latest post arrived as another demanding stretch begins. Matthew and Kelly recently spent time together in Lake Tahoe before the Rams turned their attention fully toward Week 1.

Kelly later shared images suggesting she had traveled to Melbourne ahead of Los Angeles’ season opener. The Rams are scheduled to face the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, giving the Stafford family an unusually long-distance start to the new campaign.

Matthew Stafford enters 2026 with history within reach

The family story is unfolding alongside another significant season for Matthew Stafford .

The veteran quarterback is coming off an outstanding 2025 campaign in which he was named NFL MVP and remains the central figure in Los Angeles’ offense.

Stafford enters the season with 423 career touchdown passes, leaving him within striking distance of another move up the NFL’s all-time rankings.

He threw 282 touchdowns during 12 seasons with the Detroit Lions before adding another 141 since joining the Rams.

Three touchdown passes against San Francisco would take Stafford to 426 for his career and give him another milestone during a career that has already included a Super Bowl title and an MVP award.

Kelly ’s post, though, offered a reminder that the football achievements are only one part of the Stafford family’s story.

Another NFL season means more travel, more games and more complicated family logistics.

articles.title: Sean McVay’s Coaching Tree: Full list of disciples who landed head coach jobs
articles.standfirst: The Los Angeles Rams head coach has amassed a stunning coaching tree at just 40 years old.
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams head coach has amassed a stunning coaching tree at just 40 years old.
articles.body:
As the 2026 NFL season gets underway, Sean McVay might be one of the head coaches under the most pressure around the league. McVay's future with the Los Angeles Rams is fully secure, having just recently penned a multiyear extension.

But the onus is completely on McVay to win a Super Bowl with the Rams this upcoming season. The front office has amassed something close to a super team, and the Rams are the overwhelming favorite to win the Lombardi Trophy this season. Whether McVay wins it or not, he has already built an outstanding legacy in the NFL .

McVay became the youngest head coach in NFL history to win a Super Bowl when he did it with the Rams in 2022 . He's just 40 years old now, and he has a very long career ahead of him. But what goes beyond the box score is his influence on his fellow coaches, as McVay has already developed a strong coaching tree.

Mike LaFleur the latest head coach to branch out from Sean McVay's coaching tree

McVay himself came from a fruitful coaching tree courtesy of Kyle Shanahan . Now, McVay is paving the way for his assistants, with six already having earned a head coaching gig in the NFL .

Zac Taylor : Cincinnati Bengals head coach since 2019; Rams assistant WR coach and QB coach from 2017-18.

Matt LaFleur : Green Bay Packers head coach since 2019; Rams offensive coordinator in 2017.

Kevin O'Connell : Minnesota Vikings head coach since 2022; Rams offensive coordinator from 2020-21.

Brandon Staley : Los Angeles Chargers head coach from 2021-23; Rams defensive coordinator in 2020

Liam Coen : Jacksonville Jaguars head coach since 2025; Rams assistant WR coach from 2018-19, assistant QB coach in 2020, and offensive coordinator in 2022.

Mike LaFleur : Arizona Cardinals head coach since 2026; Rams offensive coordinator from 2023-25.

There are others who worked with McVay and went on to be head coaches elsewhere, although they also had plenty of experience before working with McVay: Particularly Raheem Morris and Jedd Fisch .

Some other coaches had stops along the way, like Staley, Coen, and Matt LaFleur. But there's no doubt that other NFL franchises want " the next Sean McVay ". They just might never get it.

articles.title: Myles Garrett’s nightmare Rams debut leaves Sean McVay searching for answers
articles.standfirst: The Rams expected Myles Garrett to change their defense. Instead, the 49ers completely shut him down.
articles.summary: The Rams expected Myles Garrett to change their defense. Instead, the 49ers completely shut him down.
articles.body:
The massive impact expected from Myles Garrett on the Los Angeles Rams ’ defense was nowhere to be found during his debut with his new team on Thursday.

The two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year was virtually invisible in the Rams’ 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia . Garrett failed to record a sack, a tackle, or a quarterback hit, completely disappearing from the stat sheet.

It was only the fourth time in Garrett’s career that he finished a game without registering any of those three defensive statistics.

The highly anticipated dominance from Los Angeles’ new defensive centerpiece will have to wait, as the 49ers successfully neutralized one of the Rams’ biggest threats in a disappointing debut.

To make matters worse, the Rams’ offense also struggled to find answers. Since Matthew Stafford took over as the franchise’s starting quarterback, the team’s seven points against San Francisco marked its lowest scoring output in a game.

The loss also marked the first time since 2024 that Los Angeles has fallen by at least 10 points, raising concerns after an offseason filled with high expectations.

What did Sean McVay say after the loss?

“They outplayed us in every facet. I didn’t do nearly a good enough job. This was a humbling day for us. This will only define us if we allow it,” Rams head coach Sean McVay said. “Sometimes sports can humble you, and today was one of those days. I make no excuses. Whether you want to say it was about travel or whatever, we just weren’t good enough.”

articles.title: “The worst version of myself”: Myles Garrett slams performance after poor debut with the Rams
articles.standfirst: Garrett was held without a tackle as a lingering knee problem overshadowed his first game with Los Angeles
articles.summary: Garrett was held without a tackle as a lingering knee problem overshadowed his first game with Los Angeles
articles.body:
M yles Garrett ’s first game with the Los Angeles Rams was supposed to offer an early glimpse of what their defense could become with one of the NFL’s most dominant pass rushers on the edge.

Instead, it ended with Garrett delivering one of the quietest performances of his career and openly admitting that his body wasn't where he wanted it to be.

Garrett finished the Rams ’ 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers without a tackle. He also failed to record a sack or quarterback hit, an extraordinary stat line for a player who set the single-season sack record with 23 in 2025.

“This was the worst version of myself that I’ve put out there,” Garrett said after the game. “And I’ve got to be better. I’ve got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be, and I’ve shown that I’ve been before.”

That admission immediately shifted attention toward the knee problem that interrupted much of his preparation.

Health became part of the battle

Garrett missed significant time during training camp and the preseason because of knee swelling and tendinitis.

He practiced with a sleeve on his left leg, while Rams coach Sean McVay had previously estimated that Garrett was around 85 percent healthy.

After the opener, Garrett made clear that the issue affected more than his explosiveness.

“I was a little bit more focused on myself and trying to stay healthy than what they were doing, and that showed,” Garrett said. “I wasn’t who I needed to be for my team.”

Asked what his priority would be before Week 2, Garrett kept the answer simple: “Getting healthy.”

McVay said after the game that Garrett was 100 percent “to my knowledge,” creating at least some contrast between the team’s public assessment and the player’s own description of his condition.

Rams have to manage expectations with Garrett

San Francisco also deserves credit for making Garrett ’s debut difficult. The 49ers used quick throws and solid pass protection to limit opportunities for him to take over the game.

Veteran left tackle Trent Williams said afterward that he “couldn’t tell” Garrett was compromised because “he’s still really hard to block.”

Garrett didn't use the travel to Australia or the circumstances around the historic matchup as an excuse.

“We got to be better, myself especially,” he said. “We didn’t execute as we wanted to. We got beat on all three phases, and that’s, we have to do more. There’s a lot more on this team that can be done, and it’s tied to us as leaders.”

Los Angeles didn't trade for Garrett because it needed another solid defensive starter. The Rams acquired him because they expect him to change games.

One poor performance doesn't erase the résumé of a two-time Defensive Player of the Year, but his comments make the knee impossible to ignore.

The Rams host the New York Giants next, and the biggest question surrounding their new defensive centerpiece is how quickly can Garrett get back to feeling like himself?

articles.title: "Drowning": Puka Nacua breaks his silence on his rehabilitation and alcoholism ahead of potential NFL discipline
articles.standfirst: Isolation and pressure pushed Nacua toward unhealthy coping habits
articles.summary: Isolation and pressure pushed Nacua toward unhealthy coping habits
articles.body:
Puka Nacua’s rise from fifth-round pick to one of the NFL’s most productive receivers has been remarkably fast.

The Los Angeles Rams star now says the pressure that came with that ascent, combined with changes in his personal life, contributed to a period he describes as the darkest he has experienced.

In a pre-recorded Netflix interview with Elle Duncan, Nacua spoke candidly about entering rehabilitation during the offseason and acknowledged that alcohol had become a way of avoiding problems rather than confronting them.

“I think, one, alcohol was definitely a thing for me,” Nacua said. “Just kind of drowning myself so that the issues and the stress that I was feeling never had the opportunity to be addressed.”

Treatment, he said, finally created space for conversations he had been unwilling to have.

“But right when I entered the rehabilitation center I was able to have open and honest conversations.”

Nacua says isolation became part of the problem

The 25-year-old explained that his rapid NFL success and the birth of his first son added responsibilities he did not always know how to process.

“I would kind of isolate myself, to feel like the weight of all the issues and things that were stuck on my shoulders,” Nacua said. “Not being willing to ask for help.”

He added: “I was never one to share my fears, my worries, I was always finding different ways to escape from that tension or stress.”

Those admissions come against the backdrop of separate off-field allegations.

A woman filed a civil lawsuit in March alleging Nacua bit her and another woman during an incident on Dec. 31, 2025, while intoxicated and made an antisemitic remark. The lawsuit remains pending, and the allegations have not been established in court.

Nacua had previously apologized after making a gesture during an online livestream that was criticized as invoking antisemitic stereotypes.

His attorney, Levi McCathern , said Nacua’s decision to enter a rehabilitation facility in Malibu was not directly caused by the lawsuit, though he acknowledged that media coverage surrounding the receiver was “certainly a contributing factor.”

Possible NFL discipline still remains unresolved

Nacua has reportedly entered a pre-filing diversion process related to possible misdemeanor battery charges. Successful completion of such a program can allow an eligible defendant to avoid prosecution.

That process does not necessarily settle matters with the NFL.

The league has not announced whether it will discipline Nacua under its Personal Conduct Policy, meaning a suspension later in 2026 remains possible.

The uncertainty comes after a dominant 2025 season in which Nacua led the NFL with 129 catches while producing 1,715 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. His focus now is what comes next personally.

“I’m looking forward most to becoming a person that I think my son will be proud of,” Nacua said. “These are the darkest times that I’ve had in my life.”

He added: “As my son gets older, I can share with him some of the things I’ve learned from the mistakes that I’ve made.”

articles.title: Matthew Stafford and Drake Maye made history in an unexpected way after finishing 1-2 in last season’s MVP race
articles.standfirst: The Seahawks and 49ers defenses dominated the first two games of the season
articles.summary: The Seahawks and 49ers defenses dominated the first two games of the season
articles.body:
The first two games of the 272 NFL regular-season matchups are officially in the books, with a pair of NFC West powerhouses asserting early dominance. The Seattle Seahawks dispatched the New England Patriots 13-10 without starting quarterback Sam Darnold for all but one drive, while the San Francisco 49ers rolled past the Super Bowl favorites Los Angeles Rams 27-7 during the league's historic debut in Australia.

While both defensive units showcased suffocating prowess, low-scoring affairs defined the opening window across the board as NFL offenses battled early-season rust, exacerbated by the lack of playing time for starters during the preseason

Historic MVP Struggles From Matthew Stafford and Drake Maye

According to historical records, this week's struggles delivered an unprecedented statistical anomaly: this is the first time in NFL history that the top two finishers in the previous season’s MVP voting each saw their respective teams score 10 or fewer points in the season opener.

Matthew Stafford finished the night with just 155 passing yards , his lowest output since Week 11 of last year , along with zero touchdowns and one interception.

On the opposing sideline, Drake Maye managed 178 passing yards , one touchdown, and, mirroring his struggles from the previous Super Bowl , tossed three interceptions against a fierce Seattle secondary.

Such opening-week turbulence starkly contrasts with how recent MVP award winners fared to begin their title-defense campaigns.

Looking back at recent history, Josh Allen opened his post-MVP slate in 2025 by delivering a legendary 424 total yards of offense (394 passing, 30 rushing) and four touchdowns in an epic comeback win against Baltimore.

Prior to that, Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes historically experienced varied opening results following their MVP crowns, with Mahomes launching his 2023 campaign throwing for 226 yards and 2 touchdowns against Detroit.

As Stafford and Maye look to bounce back, history proves that early offensive slumps rarely define a true superstar's trajectory over a grueling 17-game season.
